questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose to do my exchange at Griffith University because I have visited Australia before and knew that I loved the climate and nature. The nature on the Gold Coast is beautiful and offers opportunities to go on a hike, swim in a waterfall or go surfing just a short drive or walk from home. The climate is amazing and you're guaranteed more sunny than cloudy days, The lifestyle on the Gold Coast was appealing to me as well as they have a very chill lifestyle that is centered about the nature and beaches. 

Another thing that was very important to me was that it was an English speaking country as i felt this would make it easier for me to blend in with the locals and make friends with people from Australia - not just exchange students. 

Lastly, Griffith University is known to be a very good university which guided me towards choosing it.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall experience was absolutely amazing but the struggle of finding housing and registering for classes brings down my rating.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it quite hard to find housing on the Gold Coast. I used sites such as Flatmates, Fumtree and Facebook groups to look for housing. I end up finding housing through Flatmates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Your stay is gonna be much more than just campus and classes, and staying off campus will make you feel so much more free. Everyone i met who lived off campus was so happy with their decision!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had a really hard time finding courses that would match the courses I was supposed to take at University of Copenhagen which made my registration long and stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
There was an email address you could write to for assistance, but often their reply was very slow and unhelpful.
At one point I had waited for their reply for a month and had to call them at their office to get in touch with them, which ended up costing me 250 DKK.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful, as I couldn't register for the courses that University of Copenhagen required me to take in order to get merit for my classes. It ended up sorting itself out but the process was longsome and stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When sending your first application for approval of courses to get merit send as many classes as possibly and ask them to consider any possible combination of them + start considering what classes you want and can take as early as possible and send them in for approval as soon as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was way lower than at University of Copenhagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was easier and didn't really relate that much to the actual curriculum.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Workplace Psychology 
Psychology in professional contexts
Interpersonal skills 
Sports and Exercise Psychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the course Sports and Exercise Psychology! I felt it was the only course that really incorporated theoretical knowledge in the tutorials and assignments. Also the course convenior, Tim, is really nice!

questions.answer:
Didn't really meet any unexpected costs, however I had not thought that I would be travelling as much as i ended up doing, which is why the personal spending is set to 4000 DKK. 
 
The 450 DKK for other fees covers the gym.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping and eating out was more expensive than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of different social activities available to students whether you were interested in a specific sport, activity or just wanted to meet new friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of the Boardriders (the surf club) which i can definitely recommend to anyone interested in learning how to surf and meet new friends!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can while you are there! I went to Sydney, Melbourne and Byron Bay during the trimester and then did a two week roadtrip up the east coast after uni finished.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for the social clubs!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The "chillness" of everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy every minute - it's over before you know it 
Say yes to as much fun stuff as you possibly can
Learn to surf

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start researching your courses early + look for accomodation

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living outside Denmark and being completely on your own in a new country taught me a lot! Meeting so many amazing people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Fixing my courses

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
